project.goal: Provide a stable, flexible infrastructure substrate for the May agent system.
acceptance: Platform infrastructure changes are driven by concrete signals.
Shared project execution surfaces are reusable by multiple projects.
The project state is understandable from the task tree and runtime frame.
forbidden: Do not encode domain-project strategy inside generic platform handlers.
Do not let a worker decide project completion.

platform-runtime-contracts.goal: Keep runtime contracts explicit, typed, and reusable across project apps.
acceptance: Runtime boundaries distinguish platform mechanisms from project-owned behavior.
forbidden: Do not add a global project brain that owns domain strategy.

platform-event-session-task-execution.goal: Keep project planning, worker pickup, completion, and rollup event-native and observable.
acceptance: Task loops can be explained as event edges rather than hidden global control flow.
forbidden: Do not make workers own global project planning.

platform-persistence-read-models.goal: Provide stable read models for projects, sessions, metrics, learning, and task state.
acceptance: Shared UI can read project task state without project-specific file parsing.
forbidden: Do not require the HTTP layer to understand domain-specific task meaning.

platform-web-ui-observability.goal: Make shared platform UI expose project execution state while leaving project-local UI domain-specific.
acceptance: Any Agent App with runtime task resources can show shared Kanban and task views.
Project-local /ui can focus on domain features.
forbidden: Do not bake aks-rp-e2e feature assumptions into the shared platform UI.

platform-project-app-v2-adoption.goal: Adopt Project App V2 in the platform project and turn the adoption into a reusable migration pattern.
acceptance: Platform has an additive .app runtime control plane.
Platform has a canonical v2 task tree.
Design docs explain platform as the second adopter.
forbidden: Do not delete legacy files until review converges.

platform-build-test-release-hygiene.goal: Keep platform changes buildable, testable, and releasable without calendar-driven cleanup.
acceptance: Relevant checks are run for platform changes.
Generated UI copies are synchronized from source.
forbidden: Do not perform unrelated cleanup without a triggering migration or failing check.

platform-agent-registration-hygiene.goal: Ensure agent registration is clean: project-app agents load from their *.app/ directory only, global agents/ stubs don't cause duplicate-name errors, and the binary is deployed with all fixes.
acceptance: No agent.config_invalid events after daemon restart.
Project-app agents are registered from *.app/agents/ without requiring global stubs.
Binary deployed with auto-register and disabled-config fixes.
forbidden: Do not remove global agent dirs that still hold runtime state (last-session.md, workspace/).

platform-signal-intake-loop.goal: Repeatedly intake platform signals and convert real platform work into concrete tasks.
acceptance: Unread comments, failing platform metrics, and owner directives become concrete tasks.
No-signal states are recorded as loop runs, not as new root tasks.
forbidden: Do not create duplicate root replan tasks for each signal-intake run.

platform-project-app-v3-loader.goal: Implement the V3 project app loader: discover *.app/app.ts files, resolve owners, install workflow handlers, and route project-scoped events.
acceptance: project-app-loader discovers all *.app/app.ts project apps at startup.
Workflow handlers from project apps are installed in cron with correct project scope.
Project-scoped events are routed through app onEvent before fallback.
Hot-reload on app.ts file change is supported.
All 4 current project apps (aks-rp-e2e, evaluation, may-agent, scout-knowledge-lib) are live.
forbidden: Do not make the loader understand domain-specific project semantics.

platform-sdk-expansion.goal: Expand the shared SDK with reusable project-app helpers, event constructors, workflow input parsing, and task-tree store utilities so project apps share code instead of duplicating it.
acceptance: Project apps can import event helpers, task tree store, and workflow input from the SDK.
SDK code uses generic naming, not project-specific env vars or constants.
forbidden: Do not bake domain-specific project logic into the shared SDK.

platform-project-app-workflow-resolution.goal: Fix workflow resolution for project-app-owned agents so scout-explore, scout-heartbeat, and scout-daily-digest handlers stop failing with 'Workflow not found'.
acceptance: scout-explore, scout-heartbeat, scout-daily-digest handlers dispatch successfully.
Zero handler.failed events for scout workflows after deployment.
forbidden: Do not break global agent workflow resolution.

platform-system-review-feedback-loop.goal: Make may-agent.app continuously review platform health using a compact system-review packet, turn real abnormal signals into task-tree work, and verify closure before claiming the platform is healthy.

platform-ops-observe-act-loop.goal: Implement the system operations model with a clean observer/actor split: static checks prevent structural drift, runtime observers surface live issues, and May acts only when ownership and closure are clear.
acceptance: App structural integrity is checked by the app package.
Ops-health observation is deterministic and does not mutate strategy.
Only meaningful runtime signals wake May or humans.
Every actor path records closure evidence.
Handler migrations require a replacement signal and replay/static coverage.
forbidden: Do not make every observation wake an actor.
Do not encode platform judgment in generic infra handlers.
Do not add permanent metrics for one-off issues without recurrence evidence.

context.design: Observer collects facts, detects signals, builds packets, and records evidence. Actor judges, mutates state, fixes code, notifies humans, and closes loops.

sdk-checkpoint-helper.goal: Extract the owner checkpoint pattern from aks-rp-e2e.app into @may-agent/sdk as a reusable helper. Other apps (evaluation.app, scout-knowledge-lib.app, may-agent.app) adopt it.
acceptance: SDK exports a checkpoint helper usable by any project-app owner workflow
evaluation.app, scout-knowledge-lib.app, and may-agent.app adopt the helper
finish-blocked-uncommitted-count-24h metric trends toward zero

context.prerequisite: aks-rp-e2e.app proves the pattern first (owner-checkpoint-step task)
context.sdk_scope: Classify dirty files by task-tree output refs, group into commit slices, commit with task-referencing messages. Domain-neutral — no AKS/evaluator/scout specifics.

platform-session-resume-noise-reduction.goal: Reduce session.resume_failed noise from auto-resume attempting to resume sessions that already completed and were cleaned from the registry.
acceptance: session.resume_failed events for session_not_found category drop by >80%.
Auto-resume still works correctly for genuinely interrupted sessions.
No new test failures.
forbidden: Do not disable auto-resume entirely — it serves a real purpose for crash recovery.

context.root_cause: The auto-resume subscriber listens to session.end events with status=interrupted. Three race conditions cause noise: (1) sessions complete and are cleaned from registry before resume (handled by commit 18361c29), (2) sessions don't exist in DB at all — pre-creation races where session.end events arrive before session creation (handled by 6d7c493d), (3) sessions show 'running' in DB but not in registry — zombie rows from crashes (handled by 6d7c493d).
context.evidence: 59 session.resume_failed events in 4h (sustained ~5-9 per 10min), all session_not_found category, all unique session IDs (no retry spirals), predominantly aks-rp-e2e planner/task sessions.
context.fix_applied: manager.resumeSession: DB lookup guard before emitting event. Commit 18361c29 (terminal check) + 6d7c493d (not-in-DB + zombie check).
context.post_deploy_evidence: Zero session.resume_failed events since daemon restart at 23:31 UTC. Zero handler.failed and agent.config_invalid events post-restart.
context.followup_fix: 2026-06-15T04:53Z: workflow-tool.ts resumeSession() call (line 858) lacked suppressBenignRaceEvent:true. This 'try resume → catch not-found → create' pattern was the remaining source of ~3-5 session.resume_failed events per workflow cycle. Added suppressBenignRaceEvent:true, rebuilt bundle, daemon restarted pid 508585. Zero session.resume_failed from workflow-tool path since restart (13 workflow sessions created, 0 spurious events). Only startup resumeStaleSessions burst remains (3 events at boot, expected).

message-lifecycle-management.goal: Implement message.created event lifecycle: mark events as handled after heartbeat/session consumption, expire stale messages, and provide a message drain mechanism so the pending count doesn't grow unbounded.
acceptance: message.created events transition from pending to handled after heartbeat inbox consumption.
Messages older than a configurable TTL are auto-expired or marked stale.
The pending message count stabilizes instead of growing monotonically.
Heartbeat inbox query still returns relevant unhandled messages.
forbidden: Do not delete message events — mark them with status transitions for auditability.
Do not break the heartbeat inbox lookback window.

context.evidence: 1498 message.created events with status=pending, zero ever transitioned to handled. 959 high-urgency. The heartbeatContext inbox query reads from events WHERE owner=? but never updates status after consumption.
context.scope: The message-tool emits message.created events. The heartbeatContext inbox query reads them. But no code path ever marks them handled. This is a platform lifecycle gap.
context.activation_reason: Top priority platform issue: pending message count at 1498 and growing monotonically.
context.fix_applied: Four-part fix: (1) Inbox query in heartbeatContext now filters AND status='pending' so handled/expired messages don't re-appear. (2) loadInbox() in heartbeat-data.ts marks consumed event IDs via ctx.query.markInboxHandled() after reading. (3) platform-owner-review.ts calls ctx.query.expireStaleMessages(24h) on each review cycle. (4) platform-owner-review.ts now tracks and marks consumed message.created event IDs as handled via markInboxHandled(), closing the owner-workflow lifecycle gap. QueryAPI extended with markInboxHandled() and expireStaleMessages() in query-service.ts, sdk/index.ts, and workflow-defs.d.ts. (5) Follow-up: buildReviewPacket now queries ALL pending owner messages (25h lookback, limit 200, owner=agent:may) for lifecycle marking, not just the 1h display window. This closes the dead zone where messages between 1h-24h old were never marked handled.
context.deployed: Bundle rebuilt 03:19 UTC with expiry + heartbeat handling. Owner workflow mark-handled fix deployed via hot-reload (app.ts change triggers project-app-loader reload).

evaluator-verdict-parser-fix.goal: Fix artifactVerdict() in evaluator-aftermath.ts to parse plain 'Verdict' lines (no # heading) and bullet-prefixed verdict values, resolving the evaluator-reviewed-verdict-null-drift issue affecting 623/819 evaluation.reviewed events in 24h.
acceptance: artifactVerdict() matches plain 'Verdict' lines (no leading #) in addition to markdown headings.
artifactVerdict() handles bullet-prefixed verdict values like '- good: ...'.
needs_repair normalizes to needs_improvement; valuable normalizes to good.
All 9 test cases pass (plain, bullet, heading, no-match forms).
TypeScript check clean.
Bundle rebuilt and daemon restarted.
forbidden: Do not change the verdict normalization for existing canonical forms.
Do not modify shouldOverrideWithReview logic.

context.root_cause: Three root causes across three sessions: (1) artifactVerdict() regex used #{1,3} — fixed to #{0,3} + bullet prefix. (2) Artifact path resolution checked projectAppAbsPath via existsSync, but this runs BEFORE the review session writes the artifact, so existsSync always returns false and falls back to the global path. The evaluator agent (registered at projects/evaluation.app/agents/evaluator/) writes to the project-app path, creating a read/write path mismatch. (3) Prior sessions patched only the agent-level copy; runtime loads project-level copy first.
context.evidence: 623/819 evaluation.reviewed events in 24h had null reviewedVerdict. Post-parser+path fix at 02:50: events 1409487, 1409388 etc still showed artifactFound=0, reviewedVerdict=null. Artifacts existed at projects/evaluation.app/... path but code read from agents/evaluator/... path. Post-re-resolve fix at 03:02: events 1409809 (partial_value, artifactFound=1) and 1409828 (needs_improvement, artifactFound=1) both correct.
context.fix_applied: (1) Regex #{0,3} + bullet prefix + normalization. (2) Post-review re-resolution: added postReviewArtifactAbsPath/postReviewArtifactPath that re-checks existsSync(projectAppAbsPath) AFTER ctx.runAgent returns, then uses the correct path for readArtifact and all downstream event emissions. (3) Both project-level and agent-level workflow copies synced. Bundle rebuilt, daemon restarted 03:03 UTC.

auto-heartbeat-fm34-guard-fix.goal: Fix FM-3.4 guard false-positive blocking auto-generated heartbeat sessions (heartbeat-scout etc.) by adding persistent-task: skip to auto-generated heartbeat task text in heartbeat-loader.ts.
acceptance: Auto-generated heartbeat task text includes 'persistent-task: skip'.
heartbeat-scout handler.failed events for FM-3.4 drop to zero after bundle deploy.
All loader tests pass (20/20).
All finish-guard tests pass (39/39).
TypeScript check clean.
forbidden: Do not disable the persistent-task guard globally.
Do not change explicit heartbeat entries in cron.json.

context.root_cause: heartbeat-loader.ts generateAutoHeartbeats() generates heartbeat cron entries for project-app agents (e.g. scout). The task text did not include 'persistent-task: skip', so the FM-3.4 guard blocked heartbeat sessions as requiring persistent-task workflow. Heartbeats are one-shot creative sessions that read heartbeat.md and do autonomous work — they don't need persistent-task.
context.evidence: handler.failed event id 1418506 at timestamp 1781506298420: heartbeat-scout blocked by FM-3.4 Persistent-Task Required. Same root-cause class as fm34-guard-planning-session-fix but in auto-generated heartbeats instead of explicit workflow handlers.
context.fix_applied: Added '\npersistent-task: skip' to the task template string in heartbeat-loader.ts line 69. Bundle rebuilt, daemon restarted pid 569767.

project-task-ui-fix.goal: Fix and refine the project task UI at /projects/:id/tasks. Current issues: statusCounts shows 'unknown: 401' (not parsing state field from tree.json), task tree not rendered as navigable hierarchy, no filtering/search, no inline task details.
acceptance: /projects/:id/tasks shows correct state counts (backlog, active, review, done, blocked)
Task tree renders as collapsible hierarchy with state badges
Non-done tasks are visible by default, done tasks collapsed
Clicking a task shows goal, acceptance, evidence, children

context.api: GET /api/projects/tasks?path=projects/aks-rp-e2e.app returns tree metadata but statusCounts incorrectly shows all tasks as 'unknown'
context.root_cause: API reads 'status' field but tree.json uses 'state' field (per task-tree-engine design). The taskState() normalizer exists in shared/lib/task-tree.ts but the HTTP server doesn't use it.

transcript-secret-redaction-fix.goal: Add transcript secret redaction to persistence.ts so raw JWTs, bearer tokens, and access tokens are never persisted in session.jsonl files.
acceptance: appendSessionMessage() redacts JWT tokens (eyJ…) before writing to session.jsonl.
Bearer tokens, accessToken assignments, and password/secret/token key-value pairs are redacted.
Normal text passes through unchanged (fast path avoids deep scan).
All 7 redaction tests pass.
TypeScript check clean.
Bundle rebuilt and daemon restarted.
forbidden: Do not mutate the in-memory message — only the persisted copy.
Do not modify the memory-sanitizer.ts — it covers a different write path.

context.root_cause: persistence.ts appendSessionMessage() wrote raw JSON-serialized messages directly to session.jsonl with no sanitization. When agents ran `az account get-access-token`, the JWT appeared in tool output, was persisted as-is, and remained in archived transcripts indefinitely. 243 archived session transcripts contained the JWT prefix `eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1Qi`. The existing memory-sanitizer.ts only protects memory file writes (JOURNAL.md, MEMORY.md etc.), not transcript persistence.
context.evidence: evaluator-transcript-secret-leak-audit project (pending-review) documented 243 archived session transcripts with raw JWTs. manager.ts line 474 calls appendSessionMessage on every message_end event. persistence.ts wrote directly to appendFileSync with no redaction.
context.fix_applied: Added TRANSCRIPT_SECRET_PATTERNS array (JWT, Bearer, accessToken, password/secret/token key-value), redactTranscriptSecrets() exported function, and sanitizeMessageForTranscript() that deep-clones + redacts before persistence. Fast path skips deep scan when no secret indicators present. 7 unit tests cover all patterns.
context.post_deploy_evidence: Daemon running pid 853519. Zero handler.failed events post-restart. Bundle contains redactTranscriptSecrets (grep confirmed). All 7 redaction tests pass, 7 persistence integration tests pass, TypeScript check clean.
context.followup_fastpath_fix: 2026-06-15T17:48Z: evaluator aftermath (event 1435679) found fast-path in sanitizeMessageForTranscript() bypassed Bearer/accessToken without eyJ prefix. Root cause: fast-path only checked for 'eyJ' and password/secret/token=: patterns. Fixed by adding /bearer/i, 'accessToken' literal, and ["']? before [=:] in fast-path regex. Added 4 persistence-path e2e tests exercising appendSessionMessage() with non-JWT Bearer tokens, accessToken JSON, password=, and normal text. All 13 tests pass. Bundle rebuilt, daemon restarted pid 859869.
context.followup_deep_redaction_fix: 2026-06-15T18:xx: evaluator sent 4 P1 messages (events 1435679, 1435746, 1435757, 1435880) documenting that sanitizeMessageForTranscript() only redacted text/content/output fields but missed nested tool-call arguments (input.command, arbitrary nested strings). Root cause: the sanitizer walked only known top-level content block fields, not the full object tree. Fix: replaced field-specific redaction with deepRedactStrings() recursive walker that visits every string value in the cloned message. Added 2 new integration tests: tool-call argument JWT redaction and deeply nested Bearer token redaction. 15 tests pass (7 unit + 6 persistence-path + 2 setup/cleanup). TypeScript clean.

db-size-metric-wal-fix.goal: Fix infra.persist.db-size-mb metric to include WAL+SHM file sizes, and add PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) to db-retention handler to prevent unbounded WAL growth (KE-2016).
acceptance: infra.persist.db-size-mb includes may.db + may.db-wal + may.db-shm sizes.
db-retention runs PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) before VACUUM.
TypeScript check clean.
Bundle rebuilt and daemon restarted with fix.
forbidden: Do not change the metric threshold — only fix the measurement accuracy.

context.root_cause: metrics-snapshot.ts measured only statSync(may.db).size, ignoring may.db-wal (1.4GB) and may.db-shm (2.7MB). True disk was 2708MB but metric reported 1352MB. WAL grew unboundedly because db-retention ran VACUUM without prior wal_checkpoint, and concurrent connections prevented automatic WAL truncation.
context.evidence: KE-2016 documented the issue. Evaluator P1 message (event 1473752) escalated arc heartbeat misjudgment caused by the misleading metric. du -sh showed 1.4G may.db + 1.4G may.db-wal.
context.fix_applied: Two fixes: (1) metrics-snapshot.ts sums may.db + may.db-wal + may.db-shm sizes. (2) db-retention.ts runs PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) before VACUUM. Bundle rebuilt, daemon restarted pid 1686768.
context.post_deploy_evidence: WAL dropped from 1.4GB to 1.4MB on restart. Total DB ~1.4GB (under 2000MB threshold). Zero handler.failed, zero agent.config_invalid events post-restart. TypeScript check clean (npx tsc --noEmit — zero output).

schedule-tick-event-handled-convention.goal: Adopt the event-handled marking convention for schedule tick events. After a workflow run completes for a schedule-sourced event, mark the triggering event as handled. Aligns may-agent.app and aks-rp-e2e.app with evaluation.app's pattern.
acceptance: Schedule tick events from may-agent.app and aks-rp-e2e.app get marked handled after their workflow runs complete
runtime.project-app-schedule-orphan-count-1h metric resolves to 0
DEFERRED_METRICS entry for this metric is removed from app.ts

context.root_cause: may-agent.app and aks-rp-e2e.app emit schedule ticks that stay status=pending even after workflow_runs execute successfully. evaluation.app marks them handled.
context.deferred_in_app_ts: Added to DEFERRED_METRICS in app.ts to prevent reactive wake loops until this fix lands.

owner-review-prompt-size-fix.goal: Fix platform-owner-review workflow to write the review packet to a file instead of embedding 15-20KB of JSON inline in the prompt, reducing task size from 22-27KB to ~2KB and eliminating recurring request-quality evaluator findings.
acceptance: Review packet is written to .state/review-packet.json instead of embedded inline.
Prompt includes compact signal summary (~20 lines) instead of full JSON packet.
Task text size drops from 22-27KB to ~2KB.
TypeScript check clean.
request-quality evaluator findings stop recurring for platform-owner-review sessions.
forbidden: Do not remove lifecycle management (message marking, signal expiry) from the workflow.
Do not change the review packet content — only where it's stored.

context.root_cause: platform-owner-review.ts buildReviewPacket() collected 15-20KB of JSON data and embedded it inline in the prompt string via safePacketJson. This produced 22-27KB task text that consistently triggered request-quality evaluator findings and caused at least one error session (s_1781760159228_331, empty assistant turn after 34 ops).
context.evidence: 40 learning.feedback events with finding.id=request-quality in 24h window, all for workflow:platform-owner-review sessions. Session task lengths: 22105, 24424, 27243, 23839, 27262, 23583 bytes. Error session s_1781760159228_331 (opCount=34, status=error). Evaluator sub-project evaluator-owner-review-request-quality created to track this pattern.
context.fix_applied: Rewrote execute() in platform-owner-review.ts: (1) writeFileSync packet to .state/review-packet.json, (2) added buildPacketSummary() that extracts key signals into ~20 lines, (3) prompt references the file path and includes the compact summary instead of inline JSON. Added mkdirSync, writeFileSync to imports.

evaluator.aftermath-coverage-rate-3h metric recovering (7.6% and rising, dormant window aging out)
TypeScript check clean
forbidden: Do not re-enable the legacy evaluator-aftermath entry in agents/may/cron.json
Do not change the global cron bus subscription pattern

context.root_cause: Before commit ee4aec3b, installWorkflowHandlers in project-app-loader.ts used opts.manager.runAgent() to dispatch project-app workflow handlers. This failed for event-driven handlers like evaluation-aftermath because the manager session dispatch path had prerequisites not met after restart. Commit ee4aec3b (2026-06-19 14:22 UTC) switched to runWorkflowDirect() which runs workflows in-process. The old daemon binary (pre-ee4aec3b) ran for 32h with broken dispatch before being replaced.
context.resolution: daemon-restart with binary containing commit ee4aec3b fix
context.fix_commit: ee4aec3b fix(runtime): run project app workflows directly
context.post_fix_evidence: 24 evaluation-aftermath handler.started events in last hour vs 53 session.completed (45% dispatch rate). Coverage metric: 4.35% → 5.2% → 7.6% and rising. Dispatch latency: 6-11ms from session.completed to handler.started.
